title: qa: a repeatable Studio task benchmark — "build a repair-ticket app with no code", timed, counting red errors — as the Studio UX baseline
body:
**Filing gate ③ — a task the maintainer dispatched directly.**

**Who acts on it:** pm-dispatch execution seat → a `mode:cloud` session. ⛔ Not a claim. Filed on the maintainer's word: 「用真实用户做任务测试：找低代码作者完成"零代码搭一个工单应用"，记录完成时间和遇到红色报错的次数，作为 Studio 体验的基准指标。」 and 「这个可以单卡一个云卡片推进」.

## Task

A repeatable task benchmark for Studio: one fixed scenario, *build a repair-ticket app with no code*, timed, counting every red error the author meets. The numbers become the Studio UX baseline and are re-measured each release.

## Dispatch

`mode:cloud` on the maintainer's word: browser / dogfood work that outlives a PM session. The cloud session drives the scenario in a real browser against a fresh showcase boot, following the `dogfood-verification` and checklist `RUNNER.md` conventions.

## Scenario (fixed script)

As a fresh admin in Studio: create package *Repair Center* → object *Repair Ticket* (Name text, Status picklist New / In Progress / Done, Due Date date, Problem Description long text, Technician lookup to user) → group the form → validation "Due date required when Done" → automation "notify the technician when Done" → app with navigation → publish. Then as an end user: create a ticket, move it to Done, see the notification arrive.

## Measured per run

- Wall time per step and in total.
- Red error banners shown (count and verbatim text) and 4xx/5xx answers to draft and publish writes.
- Places the author had to type JSON, CEL or a machine name.
- Dead ends: steps that cannot be completed without code (named, with the step).

## Acceptance

- The scenario script and a scoring sheet committed under `docs/qa/` (next to the platform checklist's `runs/`).
- A baseline run record with the numbers, on a named commit of both repositories.
- Every red banner and dead end cross-referenced to an existing card, or filed.
- A short protocol for 3–5 sessions with real low-code authors (same scenario, think-aloud, same metrics); the maintainer recruits the people, the agent prepares the material.

## Expected to show up in the baseline

objectstack-ai/objectui#11786 (red banners on intermediate states), objectstack-ai/objectui#11788 (Notify recipients only as JSON), objectstack-ai/objectui#11790 (Interfaces gaps), objectstack-ai/objectui#11772 (flow edges left behind). The benchmark measures them; it does not re-file them.

## Environment

Source read on objectui `main` at `82500a7` and objectstack `main` at `033e5c53`. Live observations are from the 2026-10-07 browser QA pass: `examples/app-showcase` booted with `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin` (objectstack `879bd38c`), console from objectui `179f6fe9`, Chromium 141 at 1440×900, signed in as the seeded platform admin `admin@objectos.ai`.

## Duplicate check

- Semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectstack (open and closed), *usability benchmark task build an app with no code time to complete error count baseline*: 0 hits (0 open, 0 closed).
- Semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectstack (open and closed), *dogfood scenario measure time and errors for an author building a ticket app in Studio*: 0 hits (0 open, 0 closed).
- No hit describes this.
- Positive control in the same run: *related lists action id refusal notice shown to end users* on objectstack-ai/objectui returned objectstack-ai/objectui#11768: yes.
